newsitem.title: FRANCE: France seeks to change Cr Lyonnais rescue package.
newsitem.headline: France seeks to change Cr Lyonnais rescue package.

text.p: France has notified the European Commission that it wants to renegotiate last year's bailout of ailing state-controlled bank Credit Lyonnais, a well-placed source said on Tuesday.

The source said the government wants to renegotiate the rate of interest charged on a 119-billion franc ($23.2 billion) loan granted by the bank to a state-backed rescue vehicle that took over 130 billion francs of its troubled assets last year. ($ = 5.122 French Francs)
France seeks to change Cr Lyonnais rescue =2

The loan which the government forced Credit Lyonnais to extend at below market interest rates to make it bear some of the cost of the expansion spree which brought the bank's near collapse threatens to drive it into loss again this year.
The bank eked out a 13 million franc profit in 1995 after accumulating losses of 21 billion francs between 1992 and 1994.
European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert, who approved last year's rescue package, was scheduled to give a news conference on the latest developments involving Credit Lyonnais on Wednesday.
Credit Lyonnais, meanwhile, said that the release of its first-half results had been postponed to October 3 from September 26.
